newsitem.title: UK: Formerly endangered London Zoo reports profit.
newsitem.headline: Formerly endangered London Zoo reports profit.

text.p: Britain's London Zoo, once threatened with closure because of financial problems, has posted a one million pound ($1.7 million) profit, its managers said on Sunday.

"We have moved from the horrors of the Eighties, when we had to go cap in hand to the government, into a period of sensible spending," Richard Burge, director general of the Zoological Society of London, said.
"Our crisis point which we had been building up to for 20 years, came in 1991 and since then we have turned the operation around."
Burge added that the million pound surplus is an accumulation of the past three successful years.
It is a dramatic about-face for the top London tourist attraction which had annual loses of 4.5 million pounds just six years ago.

Stripped of government funding in 1988, the zoo cut expenditures and searched for sponsorships from business. The Emir of Kuwait donated a million pounds in 1992 and another benefactor Lord Swraj Paul, chairman of steel maker Caparo, matched the sum in 1994.
The society also recently announced plans to return bears to the zoo for the first time in a decade and is planning a 4.4 million pound millennium project. ($1=.5979 Pound)
